The story is written in a dramatic script format, which means that "story time" and "real world time" (reading/performance time) unfold at an almost identical, real-time pace. This lack of stretching or compression in the immediate scene is entirely appropriate for capturing the raw tension of a brief, awkward reunion. Meanwhile, twenty years of shared history, a falling out, and a period of estrangement are effectively compressed into subtext and a few short lines of dialogue (e.g., mentioning twenty years of drinking coffee, the summer at the lake, and three unanswered messages). The strategic use of stage directions—such as pauses, silence, and hesitations—slightly stretches the emotional beats just enough to give the dialogue weight, resulting in a very balanced and well-paced narrative.
